title: Turn your collection into a researched website
summary: A collector had Manus research their design-history items and build a live website in one to two hours; they say it delivered a polished site with citations.
agent_role: Manus researched each artifact, wrote the site code and deployed it over hours; the author supplied the collection and requested fixes iteratively, sometimes days later.
outcome: Author says Manus turned the basement-collection hobby into a fully functional website with rich research and custom code
what_they_did: The InnovationTraining.org author asked Manus for a live website showing their design-history collection. They wanted research, item details and downloadable source lists. In one chat they uploaded four item photos, shared blog posts and eBay listings, and flagged items whose origins needed research. Over one to two hours Manus identified the items, checked museum, academic and niche Facebook sources, and built the site.
how_it_went: The author says Manus delivered a polished site in Wright's "Taliesin red," with downloadable research PDFs and a finished to-do list. They say it turned a basement-collection hobby into a fully working website. A replay view let them check every step.
worth_knowing: The author warns an agent may take hours, unlike a chatbot, and works best with both photos and links to compare. The post includes the author's Manus invite link.
prompt: Build a live website that showcases my collection of [type of items]. I am uploading photos of [number] items and sharing these links: [blog posts, listings or other sources]. For each item, identify the title, creator and era. Check those details against museum archives, academic sites and other reputable sources, and mark anything you could not confirm. Give each item a page with a description, its historical significance and a "Further Reading" list of citations, plus a downloadable research PDF. Use a clean, responsive design with [preferred colors or style]. Keep a to-do list as you work. Show me the draft site and your sources, and wait for my approval before publishing it.

curation.rationale: Launch seed collection, researched from search results.
